user.title: Govee API key
user.description:
Enter your Govee Developer API key from {api_url}.

This is not your Govee account password. It is a separate developer key.

init.title: Govee options
init.description: If you have RGBIC devices, per-device segment settings will appear after submitting.

data.enable_mqtt_control: Send power, brightness, and color over MQTT (faster, experimental)

data_description.poll_interval: How often every device is polled over the Govee cloud API for its state. Real-time updates over MQTT and LAN arrive between polls. Range 30 to 300 seconds, default 60. Each poll spends one request per device against Govee's limit of 100 per minute and 10,000 per day.
data_description.daily_request_budget: How many Govee cloud requests per day this integration aims to spend on polling. The polling interval is stretched automatically so the day's spend lands on this figure. Govee's own cap is 10,000 per day; the default of 9,000 leaves headroom for commands, scene lookups and device rediscovery.
data_description.api_temperature_unit: Auto (default) first uses the temperature unit your Govee account reports for the device, then falls back to converting the thermometers known to report Fahrenheit (for example H5179, H5109, H5110, H5111, H5053, H5075, H5100), and trusts the rest. Choose Fahrenheit if a reading still looks about 1.8 times too high (for example 74 instead of 23), or Celsius to force no conversion. Govee's API omits unit metadata, so the value cannot always be auto-detected.
data_description.water_detector_poll_interval: How often standalone Govee water and leak detectors (for example H5054) are checked for a leak. These RF-only sensors have no push channel, so a leak surfaces with up to this much delay. Lower reacts faster but makes more account API calls; raise it if you have many detectors. Range 60 to 3600 seconds, default 120. Requires email and password login; ignored if you have no such detectors.
data_description.probe_poll_interval: How often an armed probe (cooking) thermometer such as the H5192 is read over AWS IoT while its Live polling switch is on. These devices never volunteer a reading, so this interval is the update rate. Costs battery rather than API quota. Range 10 to 600 seconds, default 30. Requires email and password login.
data_description.mqtt_status_interval: How often every MQTT-connected device is asked for its current status over AWS IoT. Devices are largely poll-triggered responders, not autonomous pushers; this mirrors what the Govee app itself does while its device list is on screen, so state keeps updating without the app open. Lower reacts faster but publishes more per device; raise it if you have many devices. Range 60 to 3600 seconds, default 300. Set 0 to turn the re-query off and rely on what devices push on their own. Queries go out one device per second; a device whose query makes AWS IoT close the session twice is left out until the next reload (a warning names it). Requires email and password login (MQTT credentials); ignored when MQTT is unavailable.
data_description.enable_groups: Surfaces the device groups you created in the Govee app as single light entities. A command to a group is sent once and synced to all members by Govee's cloud, so it syncs better than grouping the lights with Home Assistant helpers. State is best-effort (groups cannot be polled), and group lights only support power, brightness, and color.
data_description.enable_scenes: Creates a scene dropdown per device that has scenes, and exposes the scenes as light effects. Turn off to save one API request per device at startup.
data_description.enable_diy_scenes: Creates a DIY scene dropdown per device that has DIY scenes created in the Govee app.
data_description.expose_transport_entities: Adds one connectivity binary sensor per transport (cloud API, MQTT, Bluetooth, LAN) for every device. Off by default because it creates four extra diagnostic entities per device.
data_description.enable_mqtt_control: Routes power, brightness, and color commands through Govee's MQTT channel instead of the REST cloud API, reducing latency and bypassing REST rate limits. Requires email and password login (MQTT credentials). Falls back to REST automatically when MQTT is unavailable. Experimental: it uses an undocumented channel, so leave it off if commands behave unexpectedly.
data_description.lan_targets: Only needed when LAN-enabled Govee devices are on a different subnet or VLAN than Home Assistant, so the local discovery scan cannot reach them. Enter a comma-separated list of device IPs (10.20.0.51), broadcast addresses (10.20.0.255), and subnets in CIDR notation (10.20.0.0/24, /24 or smaller). Subnets are scanned device by device, since most routers drop cross-VLAN broadcasts. Leave blank if all devices share Home Assistant's network. Advanced: if a device still is not found because its scan reply cannot cross the VLAN, pin it with device_id=ip (AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF:00:11=10.20.0.51) to skip discovery for that device. Add a trailing ! (=10.20.0.51!) only for firmware that accepts LAN commands but never answers a status read. That turns off every LAN health check for the device, so a wrong IP will look like it is working while the device never responds. Enter off to turn LAN discovery and local control off entirely.

select_segment_devices.title: Select segment devices
select_segment_devices.description: Choose which RGBIC devices to configure segment modes for.

data_description.devices: Devices to set a segment mode for. Devices you leave out keep their current mode.

configure_device_mode.title: Segment mode: {device_name}
configure_device_mode.description: Choose how segments are created for **{device_name}** (`{device_id}`).

data_description.segment_mode: Disabled creates no segment entities, grouped creates one entity for all segments, individual creates one entity per segment, and both creates the grouped entity alongside the individual ones.

error.invalid_lan_targets: One of the LAN device addresses is not a valid IP, broadcast address, subnet (/24 or smaller), or device_id=ip override. Example: 10.20.0.51, 10.20.0.255, 10.20.0.0/24, AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF:00:11=10.20.0.51
error.unknown_lan_device: A device_id=ip override names a device that is not on this Govee account. Copy the device ID exactly as it appears in the device's diagnostics (for example AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF:00:11).

confirm.title: Raise the polling interval
confirm.description: The Govee API has rate limited requests for {entry_title}; normal operation resumes in approximately {reset_time}. The polling interval is {current} seconds. Submitting sets it to {proposed} seconds and reloads the integration so it stays inside Govee's request budget. You can change it again later under Configure.

abort.entry_not_found: The Govee entry no longer exists.

confirm.title: Retry the Govee account connection
confirm.description: Real-time updates for {entry_title} are unavailable ({reason}); everything keeps working over polling. Submitting clears the stored sign-in failure and reloads the integration so it signs in and reconnects to Govee's real-time channel. If the account now needs email verification or a new password, a separate repair will ask you to reconfigure.

abort.entry_not_found: The Govee entry no longer exists.

mqtt_2fa_required.title: Govee account requires verification
mqtt_2fa_required.description:
Your Govee account now requires email verification (2FA) to enable real-time MQTT updates for {entry_title}. Go to the integration page and select **Reconfigure** to re-enter your credentials with a verification code.

The integration will continue to work using polling until this is resolved.

mqtt_token_expired.title: Govee account sign-in expired
mqtt_token_expired.description:
The saved Govee account sign-in for {entry_title} has expired, and signing in again was rejected, usually because the account password changed.

While it is expired, battery levels and readings for sensors that reach Govee through a gateway (for example an H5310 or H5112 behind an H5044) stop updating. Lights and everything using the API key are unaffected.

Go to the integration page and select **Reconfigure** to enter the current account password.
